headline: Congress named a federal building in Washington, D.C., after Ariel Rios, a 2016 law with no change to how the building works.
what_it_does: This law renames the federal building at 99 New York Avenue, N.E., in the District of Columbia, calling it the "Ariel Rios Federal Building." It only sets the official name. It does not change the building's use, budget, or rules.
when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on May 20, 2016, and the new name took effect on that date.
